description: SandboxPilot (github.com/LeanBytes/SandboxPilot) screenshot plan for MacPacker. MacPacker's launch parameters (-ArchivePath / -NavigatePath / -SearchQuery / -SelectItem / -NewArchive) are a general feature — a way to open an archive and jump to a file inside it from the command line, a script, or automation, not tied to any screenshot tool. This file is simply the first consumer: it tells a screenshot driver which parameters, scenarios and appearances produce MacPacker's localized screenshots. -DisableUpdateChecks, -ExtractDemo, -DropZone and -RecentArchives are automation/preview flags used only for the shots. An argument named after one of MacPacker's preferences (-dropWindowFormat zip) pins it for that launch only, as any command-line argument does, so a shot shows the default rather than whatever this Mac chose last; nothing is saved. A scenario has three parts: `arguments` are launch parameters and decide the app's *state*, `actions` drive its *UI* afterwards, each naming one control by accessibility identifier for SandboxPilotKit to act on inside MacPacker — which needs no Accessibility permission, and keeps this file the only place that knows what MacPacker's controls are called — and `window` names the window to capture the same way, so a shot never depends on which window happens to be largest. Identifiers rather than labels or titles, because those are translated and these shots run in every language the app ships. `testAssets` names every archive and file the scenarios use, and `{name}` stands for its path in any argument. They all live in ~/Downloads/MacPacker-Demo, the only place the sandbox can read without a file picker, and assets/screenshots/make_demo_archives.py puts them there: it generates the large handoff bundles, which are too big to commit, and Client Documents.zip with the password-protected Confidential.zip inside (password: macpacker), and copies markdown-kit.zip, which is committed to the MacPacker-TestArchives submodule because it is a real, buildable repository rather than filler. A debug build resolves them all from there by file name. Scenarios are numbered to match the media-kit frames they feed — FrameBison composes background, pointers and dragged files on top, since a drag itself cannot be simulated, which is what -DropZone stands in for. Finder integration is deliberately absent: it runs in another process that SandboxPilot cannot drive or capture. Quick Look runs in another process too, so 09-preview captures only MacPacker's window with the file selected and FrameBison composes the preview panel on top of it.

scenarios.name: 01-browse
scenarios.description: Archive browser — the handoff archive open at its root, one file selected

scenarios.name: 02-nested
scenarios.description: Browsing nested archives — navigated into an archive inside the archive, a file in it selected

scenarios.name: 03-edit
scenarios.description: Creating and editing ZIP archives — an existing zip with a file added to it and not yet saved, so the window reads 'Edited'

scenarios.name: 04-search
scenarios.description: Searching inside an archive — the toolbar filter on a source project, showing matches from every folder at once, with the field active as it would be mid-search

scenarios.name: 05-new-archive
scenarios.description: Creating a new archive — a fresh archive filled with files and not yet saved (empty would show nothing at all)

scenarios.name: 06-extract-selection
scenarios.description: Selective extraction — two files selected, ready to be dragged out (FrameBison adds the pointer and the dragged file)

scenarios.name: 07-drop-add
scenarios.description: Drag & drop — the drop-zone overlay pinned with the 'add' zone highlighted (FrameBison adds the pointer and the dragged file)

scenarios.name: 08-extraction-progress
scenarios.description: Extraction progress window at 1/3 of a large file, details expanded so the speed chart is visible (uses the -ExtractDemo preview flag)

scenarios.name: 09-preview
scenarios.description: Previewing a file — a source project open at its root with README.md selected (FrameBison composes the Quick Look panel on top, since it runs in another process)

scenarios.name: 10-home
scenarios.description: Start page — open, new, Quick Compress and two recent archives. -RecentArchives lists them in place of whatever this Mac opened last

scenarios.name: 11-quick-compress
scenarios.description: Quick Compress — the floating drop window on its own, waiting for files (FrameBison adds the pointer and the dragged files)

scenarios.name: 12-password
scenarios.description: Password-protected archive — opening the protected archive inside a delivery, so the prompt asks for its password with the delivery still listed behind it (a protected archive opened on its own shows an empty list there)
